Origin and Meaning of Yoga

Yoga originated in ancient India. The word 'yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj', which means 'to join' or 'to unite'. This symbolizes the unity of mind and body, thought and action, and harmony between human and nature.

Holistic Approach to Health

Yoga is described as a holistic approach to health and well-being. It originated in ancient India and has become increasingly popular around the world due to its many health benefits.

Benefits of Yoga

The benefits of yoga include: stretching muscles, increasing flexibility, endurance, balance, overall physical fitness, reducing body pains like lower back pain, calming the mind and reducing stress/anxiety, improving sleep quality, increasing concentration, boosting the immune system, improving heart health by lowering blood pressure, increasing circulation, aiding in weight loss, promoting overall well-being, and launching apps like WHO mYoga to support global practice.

Importance of Distraction-Free Practice

When practicing yoga asanas (postures), the mind must be with the body. This is why it should be practised without distractions; if each stretch is coordinated with breath and awareness, the practice becomes a true yogic practise.

WHO mYoga App

On 20 June 2021, the World Health Organisation (WHO) launched an app called WHO mYoga. This app contains videos and audio files to teach and support yoga practice, aiming to provide an easy-to-use and free tool for people across the world.

Practice as a Habit

We can start practising yoga at any given moment of time. However, we must remember that when we practise yoga asanas, we do not just stretch the body; the mind has to be with the body.
